title: Bird Kaomoji (・Θ・): Copy & Paste Bird, Duck and Chick Faces
meta_description: Copy bird kaomoji with a Θ beak: (・Θ・) and (◉Θ◉) birds, ( •ө• ) chicks, <(￣︶￣)> penguins, ε( 'Θ' )϶ ducks, {O,o} owls and flying ＼( ˋ Θ ´ )／ birds.
hero_tagline: Birds, chicks, ducks, penguins and owls typed in text. Tap any bird to copy it.
intro: The beak is what makes a text bird. Most bird kaomoji put the Greek capital theta Θ in the middle of the face, a round shape with a line across it that looks like a closed beak. Chicks swap it for the smaller Cyrillic ө, penguins use the rounded ⊝ or flap their wings with < and >, and ducks spread ε and ϶ on either side as wings. Owls skip the beak almost entirely and let two big eyes do the work, as in {O,o}. Each bird here is plain text that pastes into chats and captions. For bird pictures such as 🐦 🐤 🦆 🐧 🦉, see the animal emoji page.

faq.q: What is the Θ in bird kaomoji?
faq.a: It is the Greek capital letter theta (U+0398). Its oval with a bar across the middle looks like a closed beak seen from the front, so (・Θ・) reads as a small bird.

faq.q: How do you make a penguin in text?
faq.a: Use ⊝ (circled minus, U+229D) for a round penguin beak, as in （・⊝・）, or hold the arms out stiffly with < and > around the face, as in <(￣︶￣)>.
{O,o} is the classic one: the curly braces are the feathered head, O and o are the big eyes and the comma is the small hooked beak. Swap the eyes to {o,O} for a wink.
